correctness.rationale: Both 0 and log|z_1|+a are plurisubharmonic, with the latter allowed -infinity only before the bounded maximum; local boundedness plus finite max ensures continuous finite psh phi_a. The first-coordinate disk restriction equals 0 until radius exp(-a), then log|w|+a; its radial derivative jumps, so nonharmonic. For direction xi, the ridge lies inside |w|<1 exactly when |xi_1|>exp(-a); boundary equality has identically-zero open-disk slice. For Haar-uniform xi on complex unit sphere, |xi_1|² has Beta(1,n-1) law, giving tail (1-exp(-2a))^(n-1); choosing a below the stated logarithmic epsilon threshold yields the assertion. Includes n=2 and epsilon endpoint restrictions. This is an exact construction, not experimental extrapolation.
residual_risks: There is no claim about positive-measure exceptional sets prescribed in advance or smooth psh counterexamples; the ridge has a derivative jump.

value.rationale: The exact limiting boundary of a newly formulated almost-everywhere rigidity theorem is mathematically natural: zero measure is best possible even among bounded continuous finite psh functions, and the bad-direction fraction is explicit in every dimension. This gives a useful sharp obstruction to proposed positive-tolerance stability generalizations; it is not merely a recasting of the null-set theorem.
residual_risks: No smoothness variant, capacity threshold or prescribed bad-set classification follows.

final_claim: For each n>=2 and epsilon in (0,1), phi_a(z)=max(0,log|z_1|+a) is bounded continuous finite psh on the unit ball, nonpluriharmonic, yet harmonic on a family of radial complex lines of measure exceeding 1-epsilon; the exact bad-direction measure is (1-exp(-2a))^(n-1).
limitations: Sharpness only for the size of exceptional directions; no converse for prescribed sets.
Nonsmooth logarithmic ridge; no asserted C2 regularity.
